supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Energetic set with standout Good Lovin' and China>Rider despite poor tape
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers strong performances of Good Lovin', Turn On Your Lovelight and a bright China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue. Jerry opens acoustically, and Pigpen’s organ shines on the few clearer moments. Audio is noisy, but the musical peaks make it worth a listen for completists.
ai_show_review.review: May 3 1970 at Foss Hill was a free‑spirited evening that captured the anti‑war mood of campus protests. After an acoustic opening by Garcia and Weir and a New Riders set, the Dead launched into a punchy first set featuring Hard To Handle, the classic China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider pairing, and two rousing Good Lovin' runs bookended by a fiery Turn On Your Lovelight jam that segues into Uncle John’s Band. Pigpen’s organ surfaces as a high point on the otherwise murky audience tape, and Jerry even slipped in a student composition during the NRPS segment, adding a quirky local flavor. While the recordings are noisy and muffled—crowd din often drowns the band—the moments of clarity showcase the group's raw energy and give a glimpse of why this concert has become legendary among Wesleyan alumni.

best_recording.reason: Most complete audience capture; includes both Good Lovin' repetitions and the clearer Turn On Your Lovelight segment, making it the best representation of the show despite its noise.

key_highlights: Good Lovin' appears twice and is a high‑energy highlight.
Turn On Your Lovelight jam provides a memorable organ showcase.
China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue shines even through tape hiss.
Acoustic opening with Jerry and Bob sets an intimate tone.
